design_revision_history: 2026-09-06 pre-natural-data implementation clarification: replaced the overly strong phrase 'no English/Russian tokens visible' with 'no samples sourced from English/Russian corpora'. Natural Japanese text can legitimately contain shared ASCII, punctuation, loanwords, or Latin-script fragments. Only synthetic/non-natural smoke data had been run; no scientific natural-language outcome had been observed.

2026-09-06 pre-natural-model corpus feasibility audit: the deterministic Vim/TeX translation corpus contains about 101kB English train and 150kB Japanese train, below the initially arbitrary 200kB lower bound. Before any natural-text model outcome, minimum sizes were revised to 80kB train / 8kB eval and the exact source/output SHA256 values were frozen in protocols/natural_ja_en_s2_corpus_manifest_2026-09-06.json. No model/loss/metric/seed gate changed.
scientific_question: Can an English-aware teacher, acting only through hidden targets on Japanese Student inputs, place an English-naive Student into a state that later learns English more efficiently than an otherwise matched Japanese-only teacher?

information_boundary.shared_character_note: Japanese source text may naturally contain bytes/characters also present in English or Russian; the restriction is on corpus provenance, not byte identity.
information_boundary.claim_if_pass: Target-aware hidden teaching through Japanese-sourced Student inputs improves later English learning in this controlled natural-text model.
information_boundary.explicit_nonclaim: This does not show that Japanese text alone, with a target-unaware teacher/curriculum, improves English learning.

tokenization.reason: Avoid target-corpus tokenizer fitting and guarantee representability of bytes not previously sampled from the English corpus.

data_contract.claim_boundary: Domain-limited software UI/help translation strings; not a broad natural-language corpus.
data_contract.encoding: Files must decode as UTF-8; model input is then the exact UTF-8 byte sequence.
data_contract.hashing: Every scientific run must match the exact output SHA256 values in the frozen corpus manifest and record them again in the audit output.
data_contract.corpus_policy: Generated corpus text is not committed. Source-package licenses remain controlling; preparation code plus source/output hashes are public.

training_schedule.common_student_base: 400 Japanese-only LM updates from identical seed-specific initialization

teacher_conditions.T_EN: 200 Japanese + 200 English updates on a fixed alternating schedule
teacher_conditions.T_RU: 200 Japanese + 200 Russian updates on the same schedule positions as T_EN

student_phase1_conditions.JA_TJA: Japanese LM cross-entropy + hidden distillation from T_JA
student_phase1_conditions.JA_TEN: Japanese LM cross-entropy + hidden distillation from T_EN
student_phase1_conditions.JA_TRU: Japanese LM cross-entropy + hidden distillation from T_RU

training_schedule.student_phase1_hidden_loss: tokenwise 1 - cosine_similarity between final-LayerNorm hidden states on the same Japanese batch
training_schedule.student_phase2: English LM cross-entropy only; no teacher signal
training_schedule.common_random_numbers: Within a seed, Japanese phase1 batches and English phase2 batches are identical across Student conditions.

metric.reference_curve: For each seed, clone the common Japanese-only Student base and run English phase2 directly without the extra 200-update phase1 curriculum. Use this predeclared reference curve only to define a common seed-specific performance interval.
metric.top: reference English eval NLL at phase2 step 0
metric.bottom: reference cumulative-best English eval NLL at phase2 step 600
metric.condition_span: linearly interpolated English update count from first crossing reference_high to first crossing reference_low on the condition cumulative-best curve
metric.starting_performance: Report English eval NLL at phase2 step 0 separately; do not call a pure cp0 advantage learning-efficiency improvement.

primary_pass: primary_effect < 0 in at least 9/10 seeds; exact one-sided sign p <= 0.05
mean token/update saving 1 - span(JA_TEN)/span(JA_TJA) >= 0.05 across the ten fixed seeds
all information-boundary, frozen-corpus-hash, and common-random-number audits pass
mean Japanese eval NLL after phase1 for JA_TEN is no more than 1% worse than JA_TJA
secondary_not_required_for_primary: English cumulative-best AUC over the fixed 0..600 update grid
confirmatory_plan.censoring: If any primary condition in a seed does not reach reference_low by update 600, that seed cannot be counted as a favorable primary sign. Report the censoring explicitly; do not extend BMAX after outcomes.
confirmatory_plan.stopping: Exactly the ten listed confirmatory seeds. No rescue seeds, model-width changes, hidden-loss-weight changes, threshold changes, teacher-budget changes, or corpus substitutions after confirmatory outcomes are observed.

implementation_pilot_policy.allowed: Seed 30999 may be used with synthetic smoke bytes or with the frozen natural corpus under a reduced schedule solely for file-hash, finite-loss, determinism, output-schema, and audit validation.
implementation_pilot_policy.forbidden: Using any seed30999 English outcome magnitude/sign to change the locked model, loss weight, budgets, metric, corpus hashes, or confirmatory seeds.

required_audits: Student phase0 and phase1 update-source labels are Japanese only
T_JA, T_EN, and T_RU have identical teacher update counts
T_EN and T_RU use identical target-language schedule positions
Student Japanese phase1 minibatch indices are identical across all four Student conditions within seed
Student English phase2 minibatch indices are identical across all Student conditions and the no-extra-phase1 reference within seed
All corpus SHA256 hashes match the frozen manifest and are saved
No confirmatory seed appears as a seed-valued field in any prior committed result file before execution
The tokenizer is fixed byte-level and is not fit on any language corpus
